title: 5 Myths About Romantic Lopud, Croatia
metaDescription: Lopud for couples: why a day trip falls short, how to reach Šunj Beach, where to eat at the harbour, and what to do on the car-free island after the ferries leave.
content:
## Myth 1: Lopud is a half-day trip from Dubrovnik

**The myth:** Take the ferry, swim at Šunj, return by evening.

**The reality:** Day-trippers fill the village at midday. The Jadrolinija ferry from Gruž port takes roughly 50-60 minutes, depending on the line and stops. The island has only one settlement and a few hundred permanent residents. When the last boat leaves, the palm-lined, pedestrian waterfront empties out.

**Better alternative:** Book one or two nights. Small hotels sit along the seafront, including the 3-star Hotel Glavović in the village centre, and RMH Lopud Lafodia is a larger hotel on the island. Two days is enough time for the beach, the hill walk and a slow dinner. Staying over is the single best decision a couple can make here.

## Myth 2: Šunj is a hidden, private beach

**The myth:** A sandy bay with no one else on it.

**The reality:** Šunj is one of the few sandy beaches near Dubrovnik. It is about a kilometre long, with shallow water and pine forest behind it. That reputation brings crowds. In summer it has rental loungers and beach bars. Two sun loungers cost around €10.

**Better alternative:** Arrive before the first ferry groups, or go in the late afternoon. September is the better month, when the water is still warm and the day-trip volume drops. The small beaches along the village waterfront are quieter for a short swim.

## Myth 3: You must take a golf-cart taxi to Šunj

**The myth:** The beach is too far to walk.

**The reality:** The walk from the harbour takes about 20-30 minutes on a paved path, past old stone houses, between two hills and through pine and scrub. Electric golf carts run seasonally and cost around €10 for two. They also tend to wait until they have a full load.

**Better alternative:** Walk across in the morning, when it is cool. Keep the cart for the return if the heat is high. Locals rarely take the cart in the cooler hours, and the walk is the better part of the trip.

## Myth 4: The Franciscan monastery is the main sight to visit

**The myth:** The 15th-century monastery is an attraction you can tour.

**The reality:** The Franciscan complex of Our Lady of the Cave dates from 1483. It has been privately restored and now operates as LOPUD 1483, a retreat. The small church in the yard can be entered. The cloister is not a ticketed visit.

**Better alternative:** Walk the waterfront past the ruined Grand Hotel Lopud, then climb to the 16th-century Sutvrač fortress for views over the Elaphiti archipelago. Allow 1-2 hours. On the way to Šunj, the church of Our Lady of Šunj sits above the bay.

## Myth 5: A romantic trip needs a private boat

**The myth:** Only a charter or speedboat makes Lopud special.

**The reality:** A private speedboat from Dubrovnik takes about 30 minutes and drops you at the beach, but it costs far more than the public ferry. The Jadrolinija ferry costs €5.40 one way for adults in the main season (May 29 to September 27, 2026) and €3.40 in the off-season. Lines 807 and 831 run year-round, and line 831 takes cars to Šipan, though not to Lopud.

**Better alternative:** Spend the money on dinner. The family-run Restaurant Obala sits on the seafront and focuses on fish and seafood. Restaurant Dubrovnik is the other well-known option. Both are on the expensive side, so book ahead in summer. Insider tip: the ferry runs more often in summer (up to 4-5 daily) than in winter (2 daily), so check the return time before dinner.

## Insider perspective: when to go

August brings the Ponta Lopud festivals, including a jazz festival, which suits couples who want music. For quiet, choose late May, June or September.

## Planning a Lopud Trip for Two: What to Book First

Book the room first, ideally for two nights. Then fix the ferry times, because the schedule sets the whole day. Walk to Šunj early, eat at the harbour, and skip the tours.

faq.question: But isn't Lopud too small to stay overnight?
faq.answer: No. Two days covers the beach, the Sutvrač fortress hike and the waterfront, and the evenings are the quietest part of the stay.

faq.question: How much does the ferry from Dubrovnik to Lopud cost?
faq.answer: In 2026 an adult one-way ticket costs €5.40 in the main season (May 29 to September 27) and €3.40 in the off-season. The ride takes about 50-60 minutes.

faq.question: Isn't Šunj Beach a long walk from the village?
faq.answer: No. The walk takes about 20-30 minutes on a paved path. Seasonal golf-cart taxis cost around €10 for two.

faq.question: Aren't there cars on Lopud?
faq.answer: There are no regular cars. Lopud is car-free, and electric carts handle luggage and trips toward Šunj.

faq.question: Can couples visit the Franciscan monastery?
faq.answer: The complex is restored as LOPUD 1483, a private retreat. The church in the yard can be entered, but the cloister is not a regular visit.

faq.question: Is Lopud good for couples outside summer?
faq.answer: Yes, for walking and dining. Ferries are less frequent (about 2 daily in winter), and beach services are seasonal, so plan the return carefully.

quickAnswer: Lopud is not a beach stop you finish between two ferries. The car-free Elaphiti island is best as an overnight stay, because the quiet comes after the last day-trip boat leaves. Staying one night gives couples the empty promenade, a harbour dinner and an unhurried walk to Šunj Beach.
